contexts.text: Perception is a kind of internal sensation...
The external man has similar sensations to the brutes.
All sensations relate to touch, of which they are only diversities and varieties.
These scientifics... come to the sensation or perception of man...
Corporeal things have a gross sensation.
These odours cannot be sensated by man except one to whom the interior sensations have been opened.
Perception was a perceptive sensation and Knowledge of all things which were taking place in Heaven.
The sensations, etc. of Spirits are more perfect.
Divine order is terminated... in the external sensations...
The heart and lungs are the two founts... of all external sensation.
Embryos and newly-born infants cannot have any corporeal sensation... until their lungs have been opened...
(From the good of love and truth of faith) are all perception and sensation.
Spirits... have been released from the body with its gross modes of sensations.
All things there are adapted to the sensations of Spirits and Angels.

Spirits have sensations much more exquisite than men... The body, with its sensations... is adapted to uses (here); and the spirit and its sensations... are adapted to uses (there)... All the Sensitive which appears in the body is properly of its spirit, and is of the body solely by influx... Therefore when the spirit is stripped of the body it is in its own sensations in which it had been before, in fact, in much more exquisite ones; for corporeal things... had rendered the sensations obtuse...

As soon as man dies... he is raised up into the state of all sensations, and at first supposes that he is still in the body; for the sensations in which he is, lead him so to believe; but when he apperceives that he has more exquisite sensations... he observes that he is in the other life.
A Spirit... has all the sensations he had here... but not taste; but instead of it something analogous which is adjoined to smell. Explained.
The Internal... gives the External to sensate; but when it acts into the External... the sensation is dulled and obscured...
The interior man sees... in the exterior... The faculty of sensating, or sensation, is from no other source.
In the head are all the substances and forms in their beginnings, and therefore all the sensations tend thither, and present themselves there.
What good is, is not known from any internal sensation or perception.

Through the Internal from the Lord comes all... sensation. It appears that sensation... comes from influx from the external, but this is a fallacy. It is the Internal which sensates through the External...
There is given (the man who is led by the Lord) the perception of good, and even the sensation of it. AC 7442:3.

(The good of charity in the exterior man) comes to the sensation of man as delight; but (that in the interior man) does not come to his sensation, but to the perception that it ought to be so, and makes the lower mind content. In the other life, this also comes to sensation.

For all the external sensations derive their origin from the internal sensations, which are of the understanding and will; thus, in man, from truths of faith and the good of love... But the internal sensations, which are proper to the understanding and will... have not that sense which the external sensations have, but are turned into such things when they inflow. For all things which are sensated by man through the external sensory organs, inflow from internal things...
By turns the perception and sensation of good become (with the Angels) more exquisite...
The earthly body... does not receive its first sensations and motions from the Spiritual World, but from the natural world: and therefore infants have to learn...
Blessedness, with which all their sensations are affected.
From the opposite is known its quality, and degree; hence come all perception and sensation.

(The Moravians) say that they had had a sensation, and thus an interior confirmation of their dogmas; but they were shown that their sensation had been from visionary Spirits... SE 4792. SE 4796. SE 4797. SE 6043:2. LJPost 48. LJPost 279.
Thought is the first effect of life; and sensation and action are the second.
A man with whom the spiritual degree has been opened... can come into this (angelic) wisdom by a lulling of the sensations of the body...
The states (of the fibres and vessels in man) are sensations, thoughts, and affections.
From these two things (love and wisdom) in the last place, are derived the sensations, which are sight, hearing, etc., with their delights sees through the eye, (and so on).
(In swoons) there is no sensation.
What is opposite takes away, and also exalts, the perceptions and sensations. Explained.
There cannot be given to man (here) a perception of sensation that he lives from the Lord alone.
For angelic perception and sensation are much more exquisite than human...
Without permanence of delight there is no... sensation.
In merit lies... a sole sensation of the love of self.
There is such a cooperation in every sense; for the sensories of the body consist of fibres, etc... and the organs adapt themselves to light, sound, etc., whence is sensation.
Below (the animus) in the body itself, are the sensations... WE 653. WE 923.
Nothing can be sensated, unless it is from and in something; for sensation is the mode itself, which is impossible... except from a substance...
The body dies... together with those things which proximately concur to present these sensations.
He had no sensation concerning eternal life.
Those in conjugial love feel exactly whether there is what is lascivious, or not... This sensation is from the interior.
With those in conjugial love... there inflows [what is] of the wife into the sense of the husband, so that the sensations and delights themselves are communicated mutually...
The sensuous... said that they have no feeling of horror at crimes.
In the understanding is the sensation of their internal sight.
3. There must be an internal in all sensation. Explained.
The perception of the understanding thence, causes sensation.
